title: Carpet Cushion vs Carpet Pad: Are They the Same Thing?
meta: Carpet cushion and carpet pad are the same product under two names. Wills Flooring explains the types, density and thickness that matter for Sammamish homes.
keywords: carpet cushion vs carpet pad, is carpet cushion the same as pad, carpet pad density, carpet underlay types, carpet cushion Sammamish

blocks.lead: Yes, carpet cushion and carpet pad are the same thing. Cushion is the industry and manufacturer term, pad is what homeowners and most installers say, and underlay is what the British and a few product labels call it.
blocks.detail: What actually differs is the type, the density and the thickness, and those three numbers decide whether your carpet lasts eight years or fifteen. The name on the roll does not.

blocks.html: This question comes up because the paperwork does not match the conversation. Your carpet's warranty booklet talks about cushion. The installer says pad. The big-box receipt says underlay. A Klahanie homeowner recently asked us whether she needed a cushion on top of the pad another company had quoted. She did not. She needed to know which pad, because the one on that quote would have voided her carpet's warranty.

blocks.text: Why there are three names for one product

items.title: Cushion
items.text: The formal term used by manufacturers, the Carpet Cushion Council and every warranty document. If a spec sheet says cushion, it means the layer under the carpet, nothing more.

items.title: Pad
items.text: Trade and homeowner shorthand. Installers, sales floors and almost every Reddit thread say pad. It is the same roll of rebond or foam.

items.title: Underlay or underlayment
items.text: Common on imported products and in general flooring talk. Careful: underlayment also means the foam under vinyl plank, which is a different product.

blocks.note: There is no product called cushion that goes on top of a pad. If a quote lists both, ask what the second line is.

blocks.text: Density and thickness: the two numbers on the roll

items.html: Density is the number that matters. It is stated in pounds per cubic foot. Six is the floor for most residential warranties, eight is what we install in most Sammamish homes, and ten is for stairs and halls in a big household. Dense pad supports the carpet backing instead of letting it flex and break down.

Thicker is not better. Most cut-pile warranties cap the pad at 7/16 in, and berber wants 3/8 in or less. A thick, soft pad feels wonderful for a month, then lets the carpet stretch, ripple and wear at the seams. Bouncy is not the goal; supportive is.

The warranty names both. Nearly every carpet warranty specifies a minimum density and a maximum thickness. Install outside those and the wear warranty is gone before the first vacuum. We match the pad to the carpet's own spec sheet on every job.

Stairs are a separate decision. Sammamish two-story homes with a bonus room over the garage put constant traffic on one staircase. A firm, dense pad there, even if the bedrooms get something softer, is the single best upgrade for carpet life.

blocks.text: How we choose pad for a plateau house

items.text: The carpet you pick sets the density minimum and the thickness maximum. We pull that from the manufacturer's sheet, not from memory.
items.note: Loop and berber: firm and thin. Plush: dense, up to 7/16 in.

items.text: Bedrooms in Trossachs and Pine Lake get a comfortable dense rebond. The upstairs hall and stairs get a firmer, heavier pad. Bonus rooms get a moisture-barrier pad because that is where the dog and the juice boxes live.
Plateau homes over crawlspaces can run damp. A pad with a moisture barrier keeps pet accidents and humidity from soaking the subfloor.
items.note: Also the right call over a garage

items.text: Pad is stapled or glued, seams taped, then the carpet is power-stretched over it. A properly stretched carpet on the right pad does not ripple.

blocks.title: Never reuse old pad:
blocks.text: Old pad has already compressed along the traffic lanes, and it holds every spill and pet accident from the last carpet. New carpet on old pad wears unevenly within a year and keeps the smell. Tear-out and haul-away is $0.45 per sq ft on every Wills Flooring carpet job.
What to ask before you sign a carpet quote

items.html: Which pad, exactly? Type, density in pounds and thickness in inches. If the salesperson cannot say, it is the cheapest one.
Does it meet this carpet's warranty? Ask them to show you the carpet's cushion requirement. We bring the spec sheets to the house with the samples.
Can the stairs get a firmer pad? A yes, with a specific product, means they understand traffic.
Is a moisture-barrier pad an option? For Sammamish families with dogs it should be the default in the rooms the dog uses. Learn more in our guide to the best carpet for pets.
Can I feel both samples on the floor? A pad sample under a carpet sample on your own floor tells you more than any brochure. See our carpet installation page for how the visit works.

faq.q: Is carpet cushion the same as carpet padding?
faq.a: Yes. Cushion is the manufacturer and warranty term, pad or padding is the everyday term, and underlay is the label on some imported products. They all mean the layer between the subfloor and the carpet. No carpet needs both a cushion and a pad.

faq.q: What density carpet pad should I buy?
faq.a: Six pounds per cubic foot is the minimum most carpet warranties accept. Eight pounds is the right choice for most Sammamish bedrooms and living spaces. Ten pounds or a slab rubber pad is best for stairs and busy hallways. Always confirm against your carpet's own spec sheet.

faq.q: Is a thicker carpet pad better?
faq.a: No. Thickness beyond 7/16 in lets the carpet flex too much, which breaks down the backing, stretches seams and causes ripples. Loop and berber carpets need 3/8 in or thinner. Choose density first and keep thickness within what the carpet manufacturer allows.

faq.q: Do I need a moisture-barrier pad?
faq.a: If you have dogs, young kids, or a room over a crawlspace or garage, yes. The sealed top layer stops spills and accidents from soaking into the pad and subfloor, so they can be cleaned instead of absorbed. It costs a little more and usually pays for itself the first time something spills.

faq.q: Can new carpet go over old pad?
faq.a: It can physically, and we will not do it. Old pad is compressed in the traffic paths and holds odors from the previous carpet. New carpet over it wears unevenly and the room keeps smelling like the old floor. Removal and haul-away is a published line at $0.45 per sq ft.

faq.q: What pad goes under berber carpet?
faq.a: A firm, thin pad: dense rebond at 3/8 in or less, or a synthetic fiber pad. Berber loops stretch and snag when the pad underneath is soft. A plush bedroom pad under berber is one of the most common reasons a loop carpet looks worn early.
